channel.title: What NBA players and coaches have said about Al-Farouq Aminu | HoopsMatic
channel.description: The latest quotes about Al-Farouq Aminu from NBA players, coaches and executives, with context and sources.

item.title: Eric Gordon on Al-Farouq Aminu, David Stern
item.description:
Eric Gordon:

“I was supposed to sign a max deal with LA, like, right then and there. And then that’s when we had the lockout. Once we got back from that, they were promising me, 'You’re going to be here for five years,' this and that. The trade was done; it was supposed to be Bledsoe, Kaman, and Al-Farouq Aminu. And then, once they backed out of it, David Stern probably went to the GM, and they just threw me in there, and the rest was history. I was a little confused, and I was younger too. When I got to New Orleans, I wanted to do well, but I had already gotten injured. And people down there thought I just didn’t give a damn or anything while I was down there.”

Eric Gordon on Al-Farouq Aminu, David Stern, Oct 7, 2024. Source: YouTube.

item.title: Michael Malone on Al-Farouq Aminu, Moe Harkless
item.description:
Kerry Eggers:Mike Malone on @Al-Farouq Aminu & @Moe Harkless defending Jokic & Murray:

“It’s how we space the floor to make (the Blazers) pay for that. If they want to leave it one-on-one, I trust Nikola to score. If they start giving help and we space it correctly, we’ll be able to get great looks.”

Michael Malone on Al-Farouq Aminu, Moe Harkless, May 1, 2019. Source: Twitter @kerryeggers.

item.title: Brad Stevens on Evan Turner, Al-Farouq Aminu, Damian Lillard, Moe Harkless, CJ McCollum
item.description:
Brad Stevens on #Blazers:

“You start with how special (Lillard & McCollum) are offensively, but Harkless, Aminu & Turner shooting the ball has really helped. They have a lot of guys you can go to, a lot of efficient players at offensive end & versatile players at defensive end.”

Brad Stevens on Evan Turner, Al-Farouq Aminu, Damian Lillard, Moe Harkless, CJ McCollum, Mar 23, 2018. Source: Twitter @kerryeggers.
